mainTopic: The barrel משנה: whether a returned item needs דעת בעלים, whether the משנה follows one תנא, and whether שליחות יד requires a loss (חסרון).
overview: The משנה (end of 40b) speaks about a שומר who moved a barrel he was guarding, after which it broke. The גמרא shows that the רישא fits רבי ישמעאל, who holds that putting an item back frees the taker even without the owner knowing. The סיפא fits רבי עקיבא, who requires דעת בעלים. Using a 'לא מיבעיא' style, the גמרא explains the details of each half. It then accepts that the משנה is split, quoting רבי יוחנן's famous offer to carry the clothes of anyone who could explain the barrel משנה by one תנא. רבי יעקב בר אבא and רבי נתן בר אבא each try to do this. Their two readings turn on whether שליחות יד requires חסרון. רב ששת rejects both from the word 'טלטלה' and offers his own one-תנא reading, and the גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן did not accept it. Finally, a ברייתא about a shepherd shows that רב holds שליחות יד requires a loss, so לוי holds it does not. The גמרא begins to give לוי's source from the two mentions of שליחות יד in the Torah, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי עקיבא's view: the owner must know
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי עקיבא's opinion: returning an item requires the owner's knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner needs to know about it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the ברייתא the גמרא started on the previous page. It gives רבי עקיבא's opinion that a return only counts if the owner knows about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that putting an item back is enough, even if the owner never finds out. רבי עקיבא disagrees: without דעת בעלים, the person who took it is still responsible. This מחלוקת is the tool the גמרא will use to sort out the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole section depends on this מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Requires the knowledge of the owner.
phrases.notes: This is the end of רבי עקיבא's opinion in the ברייתא from the previous page, about giving back something that was taken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun on the previous daf, which sets out the two views.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, returning a taken item without the owner's knowledge does not end the taker's responsibility.

steps.title: Why does the first clause say 'did not designate'?
steps.stepSummary: If the רישא follows רבי ישמעאל, the שומר should be exempt even where the owner designated a place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the רישא follows רבי ישמעאל, why does it speak specifically about a case where the owners did not designate a place? He should be exempt even where they did designate one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the רישא follows רבי ישמעאל. If returning the barrel without the owner knowing is enough, the detail 'did not designate a place' seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא rules that if the barrel broke after he put it down, he is exempt. Under רבי ישמעאל, putting it back always works, so the exemption should apply whether or not a place was designated. Why, then, did the משנה limit the case to 'לא יחדו'?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (a question about an unnecessary detail)

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yishmael,
why specifically 'they did not designate'?
phrases.notes: He means the opening words of the משנה: the owners did not set aside a place for the barrel.

phrases.english: Even if they designated, also!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, מַאי אִירְיָא לֹא יִחֲדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי ישמעאל's position to question a detail in the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the רישא of the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי ישמעאל, returning the barrel exempts him in every case, so limiting the רישא to 'did not designate' seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה teaches the bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style and picks the harder case, where the barrel was not put back in a designated place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is saying 'it is not necessary': it goes without saying that where they designated a place, that is the barrel's place. But even where they did not designate a place, so that it is not really its place, we still do not need the owner's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה chose the harder case on purpose. If he is exempt even there, he is certainly exempt in the easier case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a place was designated, putting the barrel back there is clearly a return to its place. When no place was designated, wherever he puts it is not truly 'its place', so one might think it does not count. The משנה teaches that even so, under רבי ישמעאל no owner's knowledge is needed, and the easier case is automatically included.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes without saying (a style that states the bigger חידוש and implies the smaller one)

steps.whatToRemember: With 'לא מיבעיא', the משנה names the harder case, and the easier case is included automatically.

phrases.english: It is saying 'it is not necessary':
It is not necessary to say 'they designated', since that is its place,
but even 'they did not designate',
where it is not its place,
we do not require the knowledge of the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about why the רישא says 'did not designate'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the משנה teaches the bigger חידוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The detail 'did not designate' seemed to limit the exemption, which would not fit רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail shows the furthest case. Even without a designated place, returning is enough under רבי ישמעאל, and the designated case is included all the more so.

steps.title: The second clause seems to follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא makes him liable even after he put the barrel back, which fits רבי עקיבא. So the רישא and סיפא seem to follow different תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the סיפא: if the owners designated a place for it, and he moved it and it broke, whether in his hand or after he put it down, if he moved it for his own needs he is liable, and if for its needs he is exempt. Now we have come to רבי עקיבא, who says we require the owner's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה and shows that it fits רבי עקיבא, not רבי ישמעאל. This sets up a problem: one משנה seems to follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, even after he put the barrel back in its designated place, he is still liable if he moved it for his own use. The putting back did not free him, because the owner did not know, which is exactly רבי עקיבא's view. If the רישא follows רבי ישמעאל and the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא, the משנה is inconsistent, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: For its (the barrel's) needs, to protect it
We have arrived at (the view of)

steps.confusionAlert: At this stage the גמרא assumes he put the barrel back in its designated place. Read that way, he can only be liable because, according to רבי עקיבא, a return without the owner's knowledge does not count. Later, רב ששת (Step 14) reads the סיפא differently, as a case where he put it in the wrong place.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
If the owners designated a place for it
and he moved it and it broke,
whether from within his hand or after he put it down,
for his own needs, he is liable; for its needs, he is exempt.
We have come to Rabbi Akiva, who says:
We require the knowledge of the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended the רישא as רבי ישמעאל, the גמרא now shows that the סיפא points to רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the משנה: the רישא follows רבי ישמעאל, but the סיפא seems to follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability after putting the barrel back in its designated place only makes sense if a return needs the owner's knowledge, which is רבי עקיבא's view. That contradicts the רישא's reliance on רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Why does the סיפא mention a designated place?
steps.stepSummary: If the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא, the owner's designating a place should not matter, because he would be liable even without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סיפא is רבי עקיבא, why does it speak specifically about a case where the owner designated a place? Even if he did not designate a place, the שומר should also be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא. If it did, the detail 'the owner designated a place' would be unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a returned item only counts as returned once the owner knows about it. So whether or not there was a designated place, putting the barrel back without the owner knowing should never free the שומר. Why then does the משנה mention a designated place?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (asks why a detail was mentioned)
Even ... also (the law should hold in that case too)

phrases.english: If the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא,
why specifically where the owners designated a place?
Even where they did not designate a place, he should also be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – מַאי אִירְיָא יִחֲדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the claim from Step 4 that the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא, by pointing to a detail that seems unnecessary under his view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the סיפא as following רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי עקיבא the owner's knowledge is always required, so the designated-place detail adds nothing. Its presence in the משנה suggests it matters.

steps.title: The סיפא is teaching 'not only this, but even that'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style: of course without a designated place he is liable, but even with one, the owner's knowledge is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is saying 'it goes without saying.' It goes without saying that where the owners did not designate a place he is liable, since where he put it is not its place. But even where they did designate a place, so that where he put it is its place, we still need the owner's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the designated place is mentioned to teach the bigger point. Even in the strongest case for the שומר, he is still liable under רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the barrel goes back to its designated spot, you might think it counts as fully returned. The משנה picks this case to show that for רבי עקיבא, even a perfect return to the right spot is not enough without the owner knowing. The case with no designated place is obvious and did not need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: He is speaking in the style of 'it goes without saying'

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the same 'לא מיבעיא' tool as Step 3, now applied to the סיפא. That sets up the problem in the next step: the two halves of the משנה end up following different תנאים.

phrases.english: He is speaking in a 'not necessary to say' style:
It is not necessary to say where they did not designate a place,
since where he put it is not its place,
but even where they did designate a place,
so that where he put it is its place,
we still require the owner's knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5 by explaining why the designated-place detail is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: 'לא מיבעיא' reading: the משנה states the harder case to teach the bigger point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The designated-place detail seemed pointless under רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail shows that even a return to the exact proper place does not free the שומר without the owner's knowledge.

steps.title: So the two halves follow different תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out the odd result: the רישא follows רבי ישמעאל and the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the רישא is רבי ישמעאל and the סיפא is רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the uncomfortable result of the last few answers. One משנה would be split between two opposing תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 6 each fixed one half of the משנה, but in opposite directions. The רישא only works for רבי ישמעאל, who does not require the owner's knowledge. The סיפא only works for רבי עקיבא, who does. Normally we expect one משנה to follow one view.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
The latter clause of the משנה

phrases.english: The first clause is רבי ישמעאל
and the latter clause is רבי עקיבא?

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pulls together the results of Steps 3–6 and shows the strange outcome.
steps.kashyaTarget: The overall reading of the barrel משנה built up so far.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה should not switch between two opposing opinions from one clause to the next.

steps.title: Yes, as רבי יוחנן admitted, this משנה is split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the split, citing רבי יוחנן's famous offer to honor anyone who could explain the barrel משנה by one תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As רבי יוחנן said: Whoever explains the barrel משנה to me according to one תנא, I will carry his clothes after him to the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'yes, it really is split.' It brings proof that רבי יוחנן himself could not fit this משנה to one תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of solving the problem, the גמרא admits it is real. רבי יוחנן was ready to act like a servant to anyone who could explain both halves by one opinion. That shows how hard he found it, and that a split משנה is an accepted answer here.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not literally hiring himself out. Carrying someone's clothes to the bathhouse is a servant's job, so he is saying he would honor that person like a master.

phrases.english: Yes, as רבי יוחנן said:
Whoever explains to me the barrel
according to one תנא,
I will carry his clothes after him
to the bathhouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the split raised in Step 7 instead of resolving it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Acceptance: the difficulty is admitted and supported by an אמורא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A split משנה seemed like an unacceptable result.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel משנה really is split between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, as רבי יוחנן admitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a challenge that the next step tries to meet.

steps.title: רבי יעקב בר אבא's one-תנא explanation: he took it to steal it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אבא explains the משנה by one opinion: the case is where the שומר took the barrel intending to steal it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אבא explained it before רב: it is a case where he took the barrel in order to steal it.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone takes up רבי יוחנן's challenge. He reads 'for his own purposes' in the משנה as taking the barrel to steal it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he took it to steal it, his job is to put it back in its place. With no designated place, anywhere he puts it counts as its place, so he is exempt. With a designated place, putting it somewhere else is not a return, so he is liable. Both halves now depend only on returning it to its place, without needing two different תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: The barrel משנה can be read two ways. Either it is split (רישא follows רבי ישמעאל, סיפא follows רבי עקיבא), or, with רבי יעקב בר אבא, it is one opinion about a שומר who took the barrel to steal it and so must return it to its place.

phrases.english: רבי יעקב בר אבא explained it
in front of רב:
It is where he took it in order to steal it.
phrases.notes: This is how he reads the משנה's words 'for his own purposes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from Step 8 by offering a one-תנא reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the שומר took the barrel to steal it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to need two different תנאים for its two halves.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read as a case of taking it to steal, both halves depend on returning the barrel to its place, so one opinion can explain the whole משנה.

steps.title: רבי נתן בר אבא: he took it intending to misuse it
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר אבא offers another way to explain the משנה by one תנא: the שומר took the barrel intending to make personal use of it (שליחות יד).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר אבא explained the משנה in front of רב: the case is where the שומר took the barrel intending to use it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives his own answer to רבי יוחנן's challenge. He also tries to explain the whole משנה by one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יעקב בר אבא in Step 9, he explains the case by the שומר's intention when he picked up the barrel. The difference is the intention itself. Here the שומר did not plan to steal the barrel; he only planned to use it, which is שליחות יד.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it (here, he explained the משנה)
A שומר using the deposit for himself, which makes him responsible for it

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Abba explained it in front of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנְּטָלָהּ עַל מְנָת לִשְׁלוֹחַ בָּהּ יָד.
phrases.english: where he took it intending to make use of it for himself.
phrases.notes: Literally 'to send a hand into it.' This is the Torah's phrase for a שומר misusing a deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a parallel alternative to רבי יעקב בר אבא's explanation in Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) by the שומר's intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה cannot be explained by one תנא (רבי יוחנן)
steps.terutzMaskana: If the שומר intended שליחות יד from the start, the whole משנה can follow one opinion

steps.title: What are the two explanations arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real difference is between 'to steal it' and 'to misuse it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יעקב בר אבא and רבי נתן בר אבא gave different explanations. It is setting up the next step, which explains the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations seem to do the same job. The גמרא wants to know what legal idea makes one say 'steal' and the other say 'misuse'.

phrases.english: About what do they argue?
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי יעקב בר אבא (Step 9) and רבי נתן בר אבא (Step 10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares Step 10 with Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying legal point that divides the two explanations

steps.title: Does שליחות יד require an actual loss?
steps.stepSummary: The two explanations disagree about whether a שומר becomes responsible through שליחות יד only when the deposit actually loses value.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about whether שליחות יד requires a loss. The one who said 'to steal it' holds that שליחות יד requires a loss. The one who said 'to misuse it' holds that שליחות יד does not require a loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two explanations depend on one legal question: does misusing a deposit count only if something is actually used up?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose שליחות יד needs a real loss. Then just lifting the barrel with a plan to use it does not yet make the שומר responsible, so רבי יעקב בר אבא had to say he meant to steal it. Suppose instead no loss is needed. Then lifting it with intent to misuse is already enough, and רבי נתן בר אבא's explanation works.

keyTerms.meaning: A loss (the deposit actually losing something)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how two similar-looking explanations of a case can depend on a basic dispute about how שליחות יד works.

phrases.english: About whether misusing a deposit requires a loss.
The one who said 'to steal it'
holds that misusing requires a loss,
and the one who said 'to misuse it'

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן.
phrases.english: holds that misusing does not require a loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether שליחות יד צריכה חסרון

steps.title: רב ששת: the משנה says 'moved', not 'took'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת attacks these explanations: the משנה's wording is 'he moved it', which does not sound like taking it to steal or misuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת challenged this: Does the משנה say 'he took it'? It says 'he moved it'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges the explanations of Steps 9 and 10 based on the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations read the case as the שומר 'taking' the barrel with a plan to steal or use it. The משנה uses the word 'טלטלה', 'he moved it'. That suggests he only shifted it around and had no plan to take it for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach that? (a challenge from the wording)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet challenged this:
Does the משנה teach 'he took it'?
It teaches 'he moved it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִידֵּי נְטָלָהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanations of Steps 9 and 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations 'to steal it' and 'to misuse it'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word 'טלטלה' means only moving it, not taking it with intent to steal or misuse

steps.title: רב ששת: he moved it to stand on it and reach young birds
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the שומר moved the barrel to climb on it and catch young birds. A שואל שלא מדעת counts as a גזלן, so the whole משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, and the סיפא is a case where he put it back in the wrong place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said: The case is where he moved the barrel so he could stand on it and reach young birds. The משנה holds that someone who borrows without permission counts as a robber. The whole משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, and the סיפא is where he put the barrel down in a place that is not its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives his own explanation, which fits the word 'moved'. It also makes the whole משנה follow רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing on the barrel is just moving it and using it a little. Since a שואל שלא מדעת counts as a גזלן, this already makes the שומר responsible. רבי ישמעאל holds that putting the item back in its place frees him from responsibility, so the סיפא, where he is still liable, must be a case where he put it in the wrong place.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Someone who borrows without the owner's knowledge
The later part of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת: the שומר moved the barrel to stand on it, and a שואל שלא מדעת counts as a גזלן. The whole משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, and the סיפא is where he put it back in the wrong place.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said:
What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where he moved it to bring down young birds while standing on it,
and the משנה holds:
someone who borrows without permission counts as a robber.
And the whole משנה follows Rabbi Yishmael,
and the later part is where he put it in a place that is not its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanations rejected in Step 13 with a new reading of the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: New אוקימתא of both the רישא and the סיפא, plus a ruling that שואל שלא מדעת is a גזלן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא follows רבי ישמעאל and the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה follows רבי ישמעאל; the סיפא is where he put it back in the wrong place

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן did not explain it this way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן rejected רב ששת's approach, because the משנה's word 'הניחה' (he put it down) implies he put it back in its proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן? He holds that 'he put it down' means he put it in its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not accept רב ששת's simple solution, and answers right away. 'Put it down' implies the proper place, so the סיפא cannot be about a wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת needed the סיפא to be a case where the barrel was put back in the wrong place. רבי יוחנן reads 'הניחה' as putting it back where it belongs. Then by רבי ישמעאל the שומר should be exempt, so the סיפא still cannot follow רבי ישמעאל, and the split from Step 7 stays.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן keeps his view that the barrel משנה follows two תנאים, because 'הניחה' means he returned it to its proper place.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: why didn't רבי יוחנן explain the משנה the way רב ששת did?

phrases.english: 'He put it down' implies in its proper place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יוחנן (Step 8) did not accept רב ששת's solution (Step 14)
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defending רבי יוחנן through a reading of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's reading resolves everything, so why did רבי יוחנן say it could not be done?
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הניחה' implies the proper place, so רבי יוחנן could not explain the סיפא by רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: רב and לוי disagree whether misuse needs a loss
steps.stepSummary: רב and לוי disagree: one says שליחות יד requires חסרון, the other says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב and לוי disagree. One says misusing a deposit makes him responsible only if he causes a loss. The other says he is responsible even without a loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a disagreement between two אמוראים, רב and לוי, about the exact question raised just before. It does not yet say who holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the two explanations of the משנה split over whether a שומר is responsible for misuse only when the item actually loses value. Now the גמרא shows that this is a real argument between רב and לוי. The next step will try to work out which of them holds which side.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'sending a hand': a שומר using the deposit for himself, which makes him responsible for it like a thief
A loss or decrease in the value of the item

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav and Levi disagree.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: שְׁלִיחוּת יָד צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן,
phrases.english: One says: misusing a deposit requires a loss,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: שְׁלִיחוּת יָד אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן.
phrases.english: and one says: misusing a deposit does not require a loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives names to the question about loss that was raised in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute between רב and לוי over whether שליחות יד requires חסרון.

steps.title: Trying to prove רב's view from the shepherd case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב holds no loss is needed and brings a ברייתא about a shepherd. If he left his flock and a wild animal attacked, he is exempt. If he had put his staff and bag on the animal, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems that רב is the one who says misuse does not need a loss. A ברייתא teaches: a shepherd left his flock and went to the city, and a wolf or lion attacked. He is exempt. But if he had put his staff and bag on the animal, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof that רב is the one who says no loss is needed. Here it quotes the ברייתא that the proof will be built on. The connection to רב only becomes clear in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wolves and lions are an accident he could not control, so normally the shepherd is exempt. But putting his staff and bag on the animal is using it for himself, which is שליחות יד. That makes him liable even for accidents. Resting a staff and bag on an animal does not hurt it, which hints that no loss is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be concluded (the גמרא is about to prove who holds which view)
Tore apart / devoured (what a wolf does)
Pounced and clawed (what a lion does)

phrases.english: It may be concluded that it is Rav who says
misusing a deposit does not require a loss,
as it was taught: a shepherd who was herding his flock,
and he left his flock and came to the city,
and a wolf came and tore an animal apart,
or a lion came and clawed one, he is exempt.
If he put his staff and his bag on it, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out which side of the Step 16 dispute belongs to רב.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds שליחות יד does not require חסרון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the shepherd who put his staff and bag on an animal, read together with רב's explanations of it in the following steps.

steps.title: But he already took the staff and bag off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an old question on the ברייתא: why is he liable for putting things on the animal, if he already removed them?
steps.simpleTranslation: We discussed this ברייתא: is he liable just because he put his staff and bag on the animal? He already took them off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a question that was once asked on this ברייתא. It sets up רב's answers, which will show his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the shepherd took his things off before the attack, it seems the misuse already ended, as if he gave the animal back. So why should he still be responsible for the wolf or lion? The ברייתא needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (a question once raised on this source)
He took them off / removed them

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהִנִּיחַ מַקְלוֹ וְתַרְמִילוֹ עָלֶיהָ חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: Because he put his staff and his bag on it, is he liable?
But he took them off!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא quoted in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the shepherd is liable for having placed his staff and bag on the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once he removed his items, the misuse is over, so he should not be responsible for a later accident.

steps.title: רב: the things were still on the animal
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the ברייתא means the attack happened while the staff and bag were still on the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה, in the name of רב: the case is when the staff and bag were still on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by narrowing the case. The attack happened while the shepherd's things were still resting on the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he was still using the animal when it was attacked, his misuse had not ended. So he is responsible even for an accident. This is the first of רב's statements that the גמרא will use to find his view.

keyTerms.meaning: While they are still on it

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
It is when they were still on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The items had already been removed, so the misuse was over.
steps.terutzMaskana: The items were still on the animal when it was attacked, so the misuse was still going on.

steps.title: But he never pulled the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if the items were on it, so what? He never pulled the animal to acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they were still on it, what of it? He never pulled the animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer. Just resting things on an animal does not count as taking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To become responsible like a thief through misuse, a person has to take hold of the item in a way that acquires it, such as pulling it (משיכה). Leaving a staff and bag on an animal is not pulling it. So why should he be responsible?

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? / What difference does it make?
He pulled it (משיכה, a way of taking or acquiring an animal)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about loss yet. Here the question is that he never took the animal at all.

phrases.english: And if they are still on it, what of it?
But he did not pull it!
phrases.notes: Pulling an animal is how you take hold of it. Without that, it never became his responsibility like a thief's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that the items were still on the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Responsibility through misuse needs the item to be taken (pulled), and resting items on the animal is not taking it.

steps.title: רב: he hit it so it ran ahead of him
steps.stepSummary: רב, as reported by רב שמואל בר רב יצחק, explains that the shepherd hit the animal with his staff and it ran ahead of him, which counts as pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: he hit it with a stick and it ran in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement of רב answers the challenge. The shepherd made the animal move by hitting it, so he did take it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making an animal run ahead of you by hitting it counts as taking it, just like pulling. So the shepherd did take the animal, and while his things were on it he was using it. That makes him responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: He struck it (to make it move)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said that Rav said:
It is where he hit it with a stick and it ran ahead of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He only rested items on the animal and never took it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He hit the animal and it ran ahead of him, which counts as taking it.

steps.title: No loss happened, so does רב hold misuse needs no loss?
steps.stepSummary: The animal was not damaged by any of this. So the גמרא tentatively suggests that רב holds שליחות יד does not require a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not cause it any loss! So doesn't this prove that רב holds misuse does not need a loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof that began in Step 17. In רב's case nothing was lost, yet the shepherd is liable, so רב must be the one who says no loss is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Resting items on the animal and making it run did not lower its value. Even so, רב holds the shepherd responsible for misuse. That only makes sense if, in רב's view, שליחות יד does not need a loss, which answers the question from Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (leads into a conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: 'But he did not cause a loss!' is not an attack that knocks down רב. The גמרא uses it to show what רב must believe.
steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא thinks it has proved that רב holds שליחות יד does not require חסרון. Steps 23–25 overturn this: the animal was weakened, so רב actually holds a loss is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the two explanations of the משנה from Steps 11 and 12 to real אמוראים, so we know whose opinion each one follows.

phrases.english: But he did not cause it a loss!
Rather, must we not learn from this

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן?
phrases.english: that he holds misusing a deposit does not require a loss?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 17, using רב's explanations from Steps 19 and 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Tentative only: the גמרא suggests רב holds that שליחות יד does not require חסרון, but Steps 23–25 reject this and conclude that רב requires a loss.

steps.title: Maybe the staff weakened the animal
steps.stepSummary: The proof that רב needs no loss is rejected. The shepherd's hit with the staff may have weakened the animal, which is a real loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that he weakened it with the staff.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the conclusion of step 22. It suggests the animal was in fact harmed: the staff weakened it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 assumed the animal had no damage, so רב must hold שליחות יד needs no loss. If the hit with the staff weakened the animal, then there was a loss. That means the case fits just as well with the view that a loss is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe it means. Used to offer a different reading.
He weakened it (made the animal thinner or weaker).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up הִכְחִישָׁהּ (weakened it) with הִכִּישָׁהּ (struck it). The two words look very alike, and the next step plays on that.

phrases.english: Say that he weakened it with the staff.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 22 by reading the case so that there was a loss.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that רב holds שליחות יד needs no loss.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed the animal had no damage. Hitting it with a staff may have weakened it.

steps.title: The exact wording supports the 'weakened' reading
steps.stepSummary: רב's wording is precise. He said the shepherd struck the animal 'with a staff,' which hints that the animal was hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, because it says 'that he struck it with a staff.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the new reading from the exact words of רב's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב only meant the animal was made to move, he would not need to mention a staff. Saying 'with a staff' suggests a real blow that could weaken the animal. So the wording fits the idea that there was a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise. The wording itself supports this.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
as it teaches: 'that he struck it with a staff.'
phrases.notes: This is quoting רב's answer from step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 23 using the exact wording of רב's answer.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the animal was weakened, so there was a loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's words 'שֶׁהִכִּישָׁהּ בְּמַקֵּל', which mention a staff.

steps.title: Conclusion: רב requires a loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof. רב holds that שליחות יד needs a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the reading and closes the question. רב holds that שליחות יד needs a real loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reverses the conclusion of step 22. Now רב's case involved a weakened animal, and רב holds a שומר is liable for misuse only when there is a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. A formula that accepts a conclusion.
Misusing an item you are guarding for someone else

steps.whatToRemember: Final position: רב holds שליחות יד צריכה חסרון. A שומר is liable for misuse only when the item suffers a loss.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the support from step 24 and settles רב's view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב holds that שליחות יד requires a loss.

steps.title: So לוי holds no loss is needed
steps.stepSummary: Since רב requires a loss, and לוי disagrees with him, לוי must hold that no loss is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since רב holds that misuse requires a loss, לוי holds that misuse does not require a loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about לוי from what it just learned about רב. This sets up the next question about לוי's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and לוי argue about this case. Now that רב is known to require a loss, the opposite view must belong to לוי. In his view, a שומר who misuses the item is liable even if nothing was damaged.

phrases.english: And since רב holds
that misuse requires a loss,
לוי holds
that misuse does not require a loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרַב סָבַר שְׁלִיחוּת יָד צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion about רב to work out לוי's opposite view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי holds that שליחות יד does not require a loss.

steps.title: What is לוי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source or reason behind לוי's view that no loss is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of לוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why לוי holds that misuse makes a שומר liable even without a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It makes sense to pay only for damage you caused, so לוי's view needs a source. This question asks for one.

phrases.english: What is the reason of לוי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the view just given to לוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for לוי's view that שליחות יד does not need a loss.

steps.title: Two different mentions of misuse in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן נהוראי, says the שליחות יד said about a שומר שכר is different from the one said about a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן נהוראי: The misuse said about a paid guardian is different from the misuse said about an unpaid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering with a teaching that points to two separate mentions of misuse in the Torah. One is for a שומר שכר and one is for a שומר חנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah mentions שליחות יד for both kinds of שומר. רבי יוסי בן נהוראי says the two mentions are not the same, and that difference is the opening for לוי's source. How the difference works is explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: That is said / stated (in the Torah)

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said
in the name of רבי יוסי בן נהוראי:
Different is the misuse
that is said about a paid guardian
from the misuse that is said about an unpaid guardian.
phrases.notes: Both are in שמות פרק כב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן נְהוֹרַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question about לוי's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לוי's source comes from the difference between the שליחות יד said about a שומר שכר and the one said about a שומר חנם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a source from the Torah's wording itself, showing that לוי's view stands on a reading of the פסוקים.
